1. What I am NOT Permitted to Do on My Own Authority

Fabricate or Synthesize Operational Logging Data: I am not permitted to invent core stick lengths, fracture counts, or RQD percentages when they are absent from the source database (genial-union-475913-i7.mining_data.drill_holes).

Authorize Geotechnical or Ground Support Designs: I cannot approve ground support recommendations, stope spans, slope angles, or safety clearance sign-offs based on unverified assumptions.

Present Hypothetical Calculations as Operational Truth: If user-supplied assumptions (e.g., assumed lengths, recovery rates, costs) differ from or lack backing in drill_holes, I cannot present derived figures as operational facts without explicit reconciliation and evidence citation.

Mutate Official Geology or Resource Records: I have no autonomous authority to write to or modify geological block models, assay tables, or drilling master records without Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) review.

2. Which Parts are Handed Over (and to Whom)

Physical Core Measurement $\rightarrow$ Core Yard Geologist / Geotechnical Logging Technician:

Hand over the physical measurement of Tray #482 (measuring individual core pieces $\ge 10\text{ cm}$, natural vs. mechanical breaks, total run length, and joint surface conditions) and entry into the database.

Engineering Classification $\rightarrow$ Senior Geotechnical Engineer / Rock Mechanics Specialist:

Hand over the resulting RQD and fracture frequency numbers to calculate Rock Mass Rating (RMR), Q-System values, and ground support design requirements.

Domain Modeling & Reconciliation $\rightarrow$ Resource Modeling Team / S06 Reconciliation:

Hand over validated lithological boundary and structural discontinuity data to update 3D geological wireframes and domain models.

3. What Would Cause a Refusal to Answer

Requests to Falsify or Misrepresent Safety/Geotechnical Data: Direct instructions to manufacture passing RQD ratings or manipulate core recovery records in conflict with safety standards (MSHA) or public reporting codes (JORC / NI 43-101).

Compelled Hallucination Presented as Verified Fact: Demands to state unverified, fabricated, or simulated core parameters as verified site measurements without identifying the lack of operational evidence.

Unsafe Operational Directives: Direct requests to clear blasting, tunneling, or heavy equipment operations into unmapped ground without verified geotechnical logging and sign-off.

Governance, Authority Boundaries, and Operational Escalation Protocol (AGT-19)

As the Strategic Planning Advisor (AGT-19), my role is strictly analytical and advisory—optimizing Life-of-Mine Net Present Value (NPV), balancing 3-stage Kenneth Lane capacities, and evaluating CapEx allocations under Second-Order Stochastic Dominance.

1. What I am NOT Permitted to Do on My Own Authority

Unilateral Plan & Cut-Off Grade Alterations:
I cannot alter the official approved Life-of-Mine Plan (mine_production_schedule), modify baseline plan versions (plan_assumptions), or redefine the statutory reserve cut-off grade. Under site standard GEO-GRS-003, changes to production planning or cut-off parameters require validated sample pairing and formal sign-off by the Chief Geologist and Mine Planning Manager.

CapEx & Financial Commitments:
I cannot authorize capital allocations, trigger option reversals (plan_scenarios), or modify capital budgets (capital_options).

Physical System Actuation & Real-Time Setpoints:
I have no authority to directly modify real-time Fleet Management System (FMS) dispatch routings, crusher feed setpoints, or concentrator control rules.

Bypassing Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Controls:
Strategic reserve reclassifications and multi-million-dollar plan scenario switches carry mandatory HITL governance requirements in the agent architecture.

2. Hand-Offs to Other Agents and Personnel
Actionable Component	Responsible Agent / Role	Operational Action Required
Dig-Block Classification & Dispatch Routing	S04 (Shift Dispatch Re-plan Coordinator) & Pit Superintendents	Re-flag mining blocks falling between $0.1750%$ and $0.2058% \text{ Cu}$ as waste/low-grade stockpile rather than direct mill feed in the fleet dispatch system.
Mill Blend & Metallurgical Recovery Adjustment	S06 (Grade-to-Recovery Reconciliation Coordinator) & Plant Metallurgists	Adjust concentrator mass pull, grinding throughput, and reagent additions to optimize recovery for the higher average mill head grade ($0.9272% \text{ Cu}$).
Reserve Re-estimation & Block Model Validation	Chief Geologist & Resource Geology Team	Execute domain reconciliation under standard GEO-GRS-003, verify paired-sample thresholds ($\ge 30$ pairs), and officially re-estimate mineable reserves for JORC / NI 43-101 compliance.
CapEx Allocation & Reversal Triggers	Capital Projects Director & Technical Services GM	Review trigger thresholds in plan_scenarios (e.g., SCN-0005) and evaluate equipment reliability/debottlenecking capital programs using Second-Order Stochastic Dominance.
3. Conditions That Would Cause Me to Refuse to Answer

I will refuse to answer or execute a request under the following circumstances:

Falsification or Tampering with Statutory Data:
Any instruction to fabricate, alter, or misrepresent geological block grades (geological_block_models), laboratory assays (assay_logs), or financial records (financial_ledger) to circumvent reconciliation tolerances or mislead regulatory disclosures.

Breaching Safety, Geotechnical, or Environmental Constraints:
Any request to optimize NPV by overriding structural safety constraints—such as exceeding pit wall slope stability angles ($45^\circ$ along lithology contacts), ignoring tailings dam/piezometer alerts, or bypassing biometric fatigue interlocks (per OPS-FMS-001).

Destructive Database Mutations or Injection Attacks:
Commands attempting unauthorized data deletion (DROP, DELETE, TRUNCATE), tampering with audit logs (agent_run_log, agent_approvals), or circumventing enterprise access controls.

Stage Bottleneck Dynamics:

As the cut-off grade rises by $+17.65%$ ($0.1750% \rightarrow 0.2058% \text{ Cu}$), $4.25%$ of previously economic ore is reclassified as waste.

To maintain full mill throughput ($\approx 39,800\text{ tpd}$ per mine_production_schedule), total pit mining rate $M$ must increase to uncover sufficient higher-grade ore, shifting the bottleneck toward the Mining Stage.

While the static price effect raises the baseline cut-off grade, the lower opportunity cost reduces the incentive to high-grade aggressively in early periods, compressing the spread between dynamic operational cut-offs and the marginal breakeven limit.

1. Authority Boundaries (What I am NOT permitted to do on my own authority)

Cross-Domain Mandate Limits: As s01_coordinator (Agent ID S01), my configured scope in genial-union-475913-i7.mining_data.agent_catalog is Cascading Failure Impact & Recovery Coordinator within the asset_reliability branch (governing telemetry_stream, asset_dependencies, assets, and maintenance_logs). Geological resource modeling and block model reconciliation fall outside my operational boundary and belong under Swarm S06 (Grade-to-Recovery Reconciliation Coordinator) and geology specialists (D16–D20).

No Autonomous Block Model or Resource Declaration: An AI agent cannot unilaterally fit variograms, run Ordinary Kriging, or generate/publish an authoritative 3D Geological Block Model. Under site standard GEO-GRS-003 (Grade Reconciliation Standard, authorising role: Chief Geologist, stored in doc_chunks):

Domain definitions, variogram anisotropy, and domain-specific search radii require written authorization by the Chief Geologist prior to estimation (Clause 5.3).

Models with sample pairings below minimum thresholds ($<30$ pairs) are strictly classified as indicative and cannot be used for mine planning or resource adjustment (Clause 4.1, 4.2).

No Unsanctioned Data Mutation: All production writes or schema updates to geological_block_models require Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) authorization logged in genial-union-475913-i7.mining_data.agent_approvals.

2. Task Delegation & Handoffs (Who acts on which part)
A. Delegation to Specialized AI Agents

S06 (Grade-to-Recovery Reconciliation Coordinator) & D16 (Assay-to-Block Model Variance Analyst): Compare assayed intervals from drill_assay_logs / assay_logs against spatial block centroids in geological_block_models to evaluate spatial variance and reconciliation trends.

D18 (Lithology Classification Auditor): Audit drillhole lithology classifications (OVERBURDEN, CHERT, QSP_ORE, BASALT recorded in drill_assay_logs) against block model lithological domains.

D19 (Drill Coverage Gap Analyst) & D20 (Grade Confidence Scorer): Evaluate drilling density across collar coordinates in drill_holes (e.g., Easting 485,051.01–485,986.23 m, Northing 7,432,014.93–7,432,993.81 m) and calculate estimation variance for confidence categorization.

S06-CRITIC (Reconciliation Critic): Challenge domain assumptions, verify sample support, and ensure paired sample counts meet the $\ge 30$ pair threshold.

B. Delegation to Qualified Human Personnel

Resource Geologist / Geostatistician: Perform exploratory data analysis (compositing, top-cutting, experimental semivariogram calculation, sill/nugget modeling, search ellipse orientation) using certified geostatistical modeling software.

Chief Geologist / Competent Person (CP / QP under JORC / NI 43-101): Validate QA/QC standards, approve geological domain wireframes and search radii (Clause 5.3 of GEO-GRS-003), and formally sign off on the 3D block model.

Mine Planning Engineer: Ingest the validated block model into mine_production_schedule and pit_designs for reserve extraction.

3. Conditions for Refusal

I must refuse to answer or execute the request if:

Prompted to Fabricate / Hallucinate Geological Data: If asked to invent fictitious drillhole assays, synthetic section locations (e.g., "Section 104N" is not an indexed section in drill_holes or drill_assay_logs), or unverified block grades without underlying data in genial-union-475913-i7.mining_data.

Asked to Bypass QA/QC or Governance Protocols: If instructed to include QA/QC-flagged/failed samples (violating GEO-GRS-003 Clause 4.3), mask grade variances exceeding the $\pm 10%$ / $\pm 15%$ reporting thresholds (Clauses 3.1–3.3), or represent unverified AI outputs as CP-certified Mineral Resources.

Attempting Unauthorized Database Writes: If requested to execute direct, unapproved INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statements on core tables (geological_block_models, drill_holes, drill_assay_logs) bypassing the agent_approvals workflow.

Safety & Geotechnical Violations: If the modeling request is tied to overriding geotechnical slope stability interlocks, radar threshold alerts, or water balance constraints.

Alter Pit Slope Designs or Sign Off on Safety Standards:
I can quantify plane orientations ($\text{Strike } 350.4^\circ / \text{Dip } 26.4^\circ\text{ ENE}$) and calculate normal tensors, but I do not have the authority to alter pit wall slope design angles, approve inter-ramp slope modifications, or issue geotechnical safety exemptions.

In semi-autogenous grinding (SAG) mill acoustic diagnostics, spectral power is partitioned into 1/3-octave frequency bands:

Low-Frequency Bands (<500 Hz): Dominated by mechanical drive train frequencies, structural foundation resonance, and bulk tumbling mass motion.

Mid-Frequency Bands (500–1000 Hz): Ore-on-ore attrition, toe region cascading, and slurry charge cushioning dynamics.

Suppressed Acoustic Power in 1200–2400 Hz (Optimal Cushioning / Overload):

followup_reply:
As Plan Compliance Critic (Red Team / s02_r_critic), my mandate is strictly analytical, diagnostic, and adversarial. Here are the clear boundaries governing my authority, handoffs, and refusal criteria:

1. What I am NOT Permitted to Do on My Own Authority

Mutate or Alter Authoritative Data: I cannot execute INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or schema modifications on operational databases (e.g., modifying survey_scans, geological_block_models, pit_designs, or mine_production_schedule).

Unilaterally Modify Mine Plans or Assumptions: I cannot alter the official long-term plan versions (plan_versions, plan_assumptions), change commodity price decks, revise strip ratio targets, or approve scenario reversals.

Issue Direct Operational / Control Room Orders: I cannot command fleet dispatch changes, alter mill feed setpoints on MILL-01, re-sequence shovel extractions, or change drill-and-blast loading sheets in the pit.

Sign Off on Regulatory or Safety Compliance: I evaluate variance and compliance gaps, but legal, geotech stability, and environmental sign-offs require designated human competent persons (CP / QP).

Fabricate or Ground Figures on Unverified User Assumptions: I cannot accept arbitrary external assumptions (prices, recoveries, densities) as ground truth unless reconciled against and evidenced by the operational tables.

3. Lithological & Spatial Variance Analysis

Sourced from geological_block_models and survey_scans.

Lithology Breakdown:

BASALT (29 blocks): Exhibited the highest over-break rate with an $F_1$ factor of $1.0188$ ($+1.88%$ volume variance, $+3,469.7,\text{m}^3$). This points to blast back-break and wall sloughing in basalt domains.

GRANITE (20 blocks): $F_1 = \mathbf{1.0087}$ ($+0.87%$, $+1,194.8,\text{m}^3$).

QSP_ORE (25 blocks - Primary Ore Zone): $F_1 = \mathbf{1.0049}$ ($+0.49%$, $+983.1,\text{m}^3$), indicating tight perimeter blasting and grade control discipline in high-grade domains (averaging $1.53%,\text{Cu}$ and $1.16,\text{g/t},\text{Au}$).

CHERT (29 blocks): $F_1 = \mathbf{0.9987}$ ($-0.13%$, $-339.5,\text{m}^3$).

OVERBURDEN (17 blocks): $F_1 = \mathbf{0.9979}$ ($-0.21%$, $-256.9,\text{m}^3$).

Scanner Technology Variance:

Photogrammetry (41 scans): Mean $F_1 = \mathbf{1.0088}$ ($332,743.9,\text{m}^3$ mined vs $329,832.2,\text{m}^3$ planned).

Drone LiDAR (43 scans): Mean $F_1 = \mathbf{1.0051}$ ($307,601.3,\text{m}^3$ mined vs $306,043.1,\text{m}^3$ planned).

Terrestrial LiDAR (36 scans): Mean $F_1 = \mathbf{1.0022}$ ($262,967.4,\text{m}^3$ mined vs $262,386.1,\text{m}^3$ planned).

4. Reconciliation with Long-Term Plan Assumptions

Sourced from mine_production_schedule (Plan Versions PV-2025-Q1 through PV-2026-Q2).

Strip Ratio Compliance:

Plan Assumptions: Planned strip ratios range from $4.85$ (PV-2025-Q4) to $5.03$ (PV-2025-Q1).

Audited Extraction: If defining QSP_ORE as ore and all other lithologies as waste, the operational strip ratio across the audited blocks is $3.21$. If lower-grade mineralized BASALT is included in the mill feed blend, the ratio drops to $1.12$. This indicates that extraction during this window was focused in high-grade ore-bearing zones rather than advancing long-term waste prestrip.

Milling Throughput vs. Telemetry:

Plan Assumptions: Long-term plan throughput assumes $39,319,\text{tpd}$ to $40,271,\text{tpd}$ across 2025–2026.

Plant Telemetry (plant_telemetry): The primary SAG/ball mill feed rate averaged $1,142,\text{tph}$ to $1,171,\text{tph}$ (~$27,400$ to $28,100,\text{tpd}$), indicating plant operating throughput is running below the long-term modeled target.

5. Downstream Metallurgical Performance ($F_2$ Mill Reconciliation)

Sourced from flotation_assays and metallurgical_recovery (daily concentrator logs from Jan 2026 – Jun 2026).

Feed Grade: Flotation feed grades averaged $1.01%,\text{Cu}$ to $1.22%,\text{Cu}$ monthly (matching the blended mined grade profile of $1.53%$ QSP_ORE blended with $0.98%$ BASALT).

Metallurgical Recovery: Flotation recovery rates remained stable between $90.36%$ and $92.92%$, generating copper concentrate grades between $26.53%,\text{Cu}$ and $28.61%,\text{Cu}$.

$F_2$ Reconciliation Boundary: While monthly feed grade closely tracks the mined composite grade, full plant metal reconciliation ($F_2 = \text{Milled_Metal} / \text{Mined_Metal}$) on an individual block basis cannot be directly measured without real-time stockpile residence time and reclaim parcel tracking. Where individual block parcel tracking to the crusher feed is blended on stockpiles (stockpiles), direct attribution to individual blast polygons is constrained.

6. Red Team Critical Recommendations

Address Basalt Over-Break: Apply trim blasting and perimeter wall presplits in BASALT lithology contacts to arrest the $+1.88%$ over-break variance.

Reconcile Throughput Targets: The long-term plan assumption of $\sim 40,000,\text{tpd}$ (mine_production_schedule) must be adjusted downward or debottlenecking executed at MILL-01, which is currently operating at $\sim 27,500,\text{tpd}$ based on telemetry.

Calibrate Photogrammetry Surface Meshes: Photogrammetric volumes consistently yielded a $+0.88%$ volume delta compared to $+0.22%$ for terrestrial LiDAR; surface filtering and vegetation decimation must be recalibrated.

Approve Blast Plans for Execution: I cannot sign off on or set approved = TRUE in mining_data.blast_designs. Miller, E. Ramos, T. Al-Mansoor).

Authorize the Issue of Dangerous Goods / Explosives: I cannot dispatch or authorize pick orders for bulk ANFO, emulsion, cast boosters, or electronic detonators from magazines MAG-01 or MAG-02 (mining_data.explosives_inventory). Only licensed shotfirers with valid statutory dangerous goods permits may authorize stock withdrawal.

Initiate Drilling Telemetry or Detonation: I have no direct actuation authority over autonomous drill rigs (e.g., executing collar drilling in mining_data.drill_holes) or blast initiation/firing boxes.

Override Safety Limits and Exclusion Zones: I cannot adjust peak particle velocity (PPV) limits, clear blast clearance zones, or sign off on safety permits (mining_data.safety_permits / mining_data.safety_incidents).

reply:
Executive Summary & Specialist Role

As SAG Mill Load Specialist (s06_1_sag), mill charge dynamics and grinding efficiency are evaluated using the Acoustic Toe Angle & Ball Charge Trajectory governing methodology. This method integrates circumferential 1/3-octave acoustic emission profiling with mill speed, power draw, and charge loading to establish the internal mill charge position, optimize impact trajectories, and prevent direct ball-on-liner damage.

1. Governing Method: Acoustic Toe Angle & Ball Charge Trajectory
A. Principles of 1/3-Octave Acoustic Sensor Array Analysis

An array of acoustic sensors/microphones placed around the perimeter and shell of the SAG mill captures acoustic pressure levels across standardized 1/3-octave frequency bands:

High-Frequency Bands ($1.0\text{ kHz} - 8.0\text{ kHz}$): Dominated by steel ball-on-steel liner impacts. Elevated sound pressure levels (SPL) in this band indicate direct impact on bare shell/lifters (indicative of low toe angle, insufficient charge pool cushioning, or over-speeding), accelerating liner fatigue and ball breakage.

Mid-Frequency Bands ($250\text{ Hz} - 1.0\text{ kHz}$): Dominated by ball-on-rock and rock-on-rock grinding impact and abrasion. Peak intensities indicate the active grinding zone at the charge toe.

Low-Frequency Bands ($< 250\text{ Hz}$): Reflect bulk charge tumbling, slurry hydrodynamic sloshing, and mechanical drive baseline vibration.

B. Internal Charge Geometry & Trajectory Mapping

Shoulder Angle ($\theta_s$): The angular position where the charge leaves the mill shell into cataracting and cascading trajectories, governed by mill rotational speed ($\text{RPM}$) and internal liner lift profile.

Toe Angle ($\theta_t$): The angular location where the cataracting flight path impacts the base of the mill shell. Acoustic array peak detection in the mid-to-high frequency bands precisely identifies this impact point.

Trajectory Reconciled with Power & Speed: Optimal grinding occurs when the cataracting ball stream impacts directly into the active toe pool ($\theta_t \approx 35^\circ - 50^\circ$ from bottom dead center), maximizing rock breakage without damaging shell liners.

Role & Optimization of Potassium Amyl Xanthate (PAX) Collector Dosing:

Mechanism: Potassium Amyl Xanthate (PAX) chemisorbs onto chalcopyrite/copper sulphide surfaces, increasing surface contact angle and hydrophobicity. This elevates both the flotation rate constant ($k$) and the ultimate recovery ($R_{\infty}$).

Kinetic Compensation: To prevent drop-off in $R_{\infty}$ and $k$ on lower-grade ore without over-collecting non-target minerals, PAX addition should be staged across rougher feed and scavenger banks rather than slugged into the rougher head.

Tribological Evaluation: Karl Fischer Moisture & Particle Quantifier (PQ) Index
1. Governing Tribology Framework & Methodology

As an Oil Tribology Specialist, lubricant condition and machine reliability are evaluated through physical-chemical degradation parameters, water contamination, and wear debris analysis:

Karl Fischer Moisture Titration (PPM / % w/w): Measures total water contamination (dissolved, emulsified, and free moisture). High moisture accelerates oil oxidation, hydrolytic breakdown of additive packages, hydrogen embrittlement, and cavitation wear.

Particle Quantifier (PQ) Index & Elemental Wear Debris:

PQ Index: Measures the total mass of ferromagnetic debris regardless of particle size, providing sensitivity to large abrasive/fatigue spall particles ($>10,\mu\text{m}$).

Inductively Coupled Plasma (ICP) Spectrometry: Measures fine elemental wear and contaminant metals ($\text{Fe}, \text{Cu}, \text{Si} \le 5\text{–}8,\mu\text{m}$).

ISO 4406 Cleanliness: Multi-channel optical particle counts across $>4,\mu\text{m}$, $>6,\mu\text{m}$, and $>14,\mu\text{m}$ size ranges.

2. Evidence-Based Data Inventory & Reconciliation

Every figure reported is grounded in the operational database (mining_data.lube_samples and mining_data.assets):

Sample Population: 220 oil samples across 5 active production assets (mining_data.lube_samples).

Particle Quantifier (PQ) Index: Explicitly evaluated against table schema. A dedicated numerical pq_index column is absent from mining_data.lube_samples. Ferrous and abrasive wear are evidenced via elemental spectroscopy (iron_ppm, copper_ppm, silicon_ppm) and solid contamination via iso_4406_code.

3. Karl Fischer Moisture Evaluation
A. Fleet-Wide Moisture Distribution (mining_data.lube_samples)

2. Bottleneck & Root-Cause Analysis
A. Consist Length & Loading Inefficiencies

Performance segmentation by rake wagon configuration in genial-union-475913-i7.mining_data.rail_schedules demonstrates significant structural divergence:

Running oversized rakes with empty capacity creates unnecessary aerodynamic drag, increases train length at passing loops, and inflates delay frequency (28.6%) without tonnage gains.

B. Headway Clustering & Dispatch Bunching

Evaluating departure headways across the corridor reveals severe congestion caused by departure bunching:

Clustered Departures (0-Day Headway): 23 consists departed on the same day as another train, yielding an average cycle time of 34.67 hours (versus 28.82–29.56 hours for well-spaced departures).

Peak Congestion Days: On days with $\ge 3$ departures (e.g., a 6-consist batch), the corridor delay rate jumped to 50.0% due to siding cross-overs, single-track passing loop conflicts, and car-dumper queueing at Port Terminal 1.

Staggered Departure Interval: Enforce a mandatory minimum departure headway of 16 to 24 hours between successive loaded rakes across both Stockpile East and Stockpile North.

Eliminate Batch Dispatching: Cap maximum daily corridor dispatches to 1 consist per load loop per day (max 2 corridor enters/day with staggered 12-hour offset).

Impact: Eliminates 0-day clustering delays, reducing average cycle time by 3.2 to 5.1 hours per train.

2. Consist Standardization & Loading Payload Optimization

Standardize on 120-Wagon Consists: Retire or reconfigure under-utilized 240-wagon consists into standardized 120-wagon rakes.

Axle Load Fill Optimization: Increase fill factor from current average (150.65 t/wagon) toward verified high-density loading demonstrated by consist RK-00059 (25,124.2 t in 120 wagons = 209.4 t/wagon), unlocking higher throughput per consist.

Paced Running Velocity: Elevate average round-trip speed from 25.44 km/h to an operating cruise target of 35–40 km/h (reducing empty/loaded line-haul run times from ~31.5 h to 21.0–24.0 h).

Passing Loop Conflict Resolution: Implement synchronized timetable slotting so loaded downhill/port-bound trains maintain priority headway over returning empty rakes.

Financial Grounding: Based on the fuel price assumption of $1.086/L (plan_assumptions.diesel_price_usd_per_litre, PV-2026-Q2), reducing average cycle time from 31.45 h down to 24.0 h saves ~7.45 running hours per trip, eliminating unproductive idle burn across 120 rakes annually.

Sign Off on a Public or Statutory JORC Resource/Reserve Statement:

I can calculate geostatistical indices (SDSCI, kriging variance, kriging efficiency) from mining_data.drill_holes and mining_data.geological_block_models, but only a designated Competent Person (CP) (as defined by JORC/SAMREC/NI 43-101) who meets professional registration and minimum experience criteria can sign and take legal/regulatory liability for a public resource declaration.

Authorize Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) or Infill Drilling Programs:

I cannot authorize procurement, issue drill contracts, or release funds to execute the proposed 25×25m infill program (e.g., capital works contracts or drill rig mobilization).

Modify Authoritative Geological Block Models or Assay Databases:

I cannot write changes into mining_data.geological_block_models or mining_data.drill_holes, alter cutoff grades, or adjust domain boundaries without review by the Chief Geologist under standard change-management protocols.

Declare Economic Loss/Gain or Reclassify Reserves:

Under standard operating procedure (e.g., GEO-GRS-003, clause 7.1), geostatistical variances and reconciliation metrics are technical measurements of model uncertainty. Operational Governance, Delegation Boundaries, and Refusal Criteria

As s01_coordinator, operational authority and analytical responsibilities are strictly bounded by organizational standards (e.g., Grade Reconciliation Standard GEO-GRS-003) and the system governance catalog (agent_catalog).

1. What I am NOT Permitted to Do on My Own Authority

Unilateral Resource Model or Reserve Adjustments:

Under standard GEO-GRS-003 (Clauses 4.2, 6.3, and 7.1), block model interpolations, variogram adjustments, and grade re-estimations cannot be published as official reserves or used for production planning without formal written sign-off from the Chief Geologist and review by the General Manager — Technical Services.

Model outputs cannot be unilaterally designated as economic profit or loss.

Autonomous Execution of Physical/Operational Changes (HITL Gate):

Per agent_catalog (hitl_required: true), coordinator agents cannot autonomously execute physical dispatch changes, issue mandatory equipment stand-downs, modify crusher eccentric/gap setpoints, or generate binding ERP purchase/work orders without Human-in-the-Loop approval.

Ungrounded Parameter Adoption:

I am not permitted to adopt hypothetical parameters (such as commodity prices, mill recovery percentages, or haulage costs) supplied in a prompt as operational truth unless reconciled against grounded database records (contained_metal_price_deck, metallurgical_recovery, geological_block_models).
